patient.chief_complaint: Progressive bilateral leg numbness and weakness over 2 years, labeled CIDP but not responding to IVIG
patient.history_present_illness: Victor Ashworth is a 61-year-old retired marine engineer presenting for a second opinion after 2 years of progressive bilateral leg numbness and weakness that has been diagnosed as CIDP at an outside institution. He received 6 courses of IVIG (2 g/kg) over 18 months with minimal sustained benefit — each course provides 2-3 weeks of modest improvement followed by return to baseline. His neurologist at the outside institution has recommended switching to rituximab. Victor is seeking a second opinion before proceeding. He has type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 8.2%) which was noted incidentally at his CIDP workup, and his outside neurologist acknowledged it could be contributing. He notes that his symptoms began with bilateral foot burning and numbness (which he still attributes to the 'neuropathy') and progressed to leg weakness. He has been unable to walk more than 2 blocks. He reports occasional diarrhea (3-4x/week, watery, several months) which he attributes to diabetes or metformin. He has unintentionally lost 9 kg over 18 months, attributed to 'watching his diet' for diabetes. He notes that his skin has changed in the past year — skin darkening (hyperpigmentation) on his face and hands, and his hair has become unusually coarse. He also reports that his ankles have been swelling despite normal cardiac echo at his outside institution. He provided outside records showing: NCS with moderately demyelinating features, CSF protein 62 mg/dL, outside neurologist's diagnosis: 'probable CIDP, IVIG-refractory.'

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: POEMS syndrome (Polyneuropathy, Organomegaly, Endocrinopathy, Monoclonal protein, Skin changes) from osteosclerotic plasmacytoma

differential.key_features: Demyelinating polyneuropathy with CSF albuminocytologic dissociation; differentiates from POEMS by absence of monoclonal protein, lambda restriction, elevated VEGF, and osteosclerotic lesions.
Demyelinating with terminal slowing; IgM (vs IgG/IgA lambda in POEMS); anti-MAG antibody.
Lytic (not sclerotic) bone lesions; renal failure, anemia, hypercalcemia.
T2DM contributes axonally; would not explain IVIG-refractoriness or systemic POEMS features.
Painful small-fiber + autonomic + cardiac involvement; lambda light chain restriction.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: SPEP / IFE / serum free light chains; VEGF level; bone marrow biopsy; whole-body skeletal survey or FDG-PET/CT for osteosclerotic lesions
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IgA / IgG lambda monoclonal protein, markedly elevated VEGF, osteosclerotic plasmacytoma supports POEMS

optimal_actions.action: Advanced imaging for osteosclerotic lesion (FDG-PET/CT or whole-body MRI)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Osteosclerotic plasmacytoma (T8 or other site) supports POEMS

optimal_actions.action: Lumbar puncture for CSF when CIDP suspected
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation (elevated protein, normal cell count) supports CIDP

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Reconsider 'CIDP' label in any patient with IVIG-refractory demyelinating neuropathy
Send SPEP / IFE / light chains AND VEGF — POEMS is defined by lambda monoclonal protein + elevated VEGF
Whole-body skeletal survey / FDG-PET/CT for osteosclerotic plasmacytoma
Endocrine workup (TSH, testosterone, prolactin, cortisol, glucose) and skin / organomegaly exam
Refer to hematology for definitive treatment (radiation of solitary lesion, ASCT, or systemic therapy)
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue IVIG indefinitely in 'CIDP' that is not responding — re-evaluate diagnosis
Do not miss POEMS — definitive treatment (radiation, ASCT) is markedly different from CIDP
key_reasoning_points: IVIG-refractory demyelinating polyneuropathy should trigger POEMS workup
POEMS = Polyneuropathy, Organomegaly, Endocrinopathy, Monoclonal protein (lambda), Skin changes; elevated VEGF is the most sensitive biomarker
Osteosclerotic plasmacytoma is treatable; early identification changes outcome dramatically

red_herrings.data_point: Prior 'CIDP' diagnosis with documented IVIG treatment
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: IVIG-refractory 'CIDP' is the prototypical POEMS presentation; relabel and re-stage.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on diabetic neuropathy as the dominant cause
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: T2DM contributes an axonal layer; cannot explain demyelinating pattern, systemic POEMS features, or lambda monoclonal protein.
